options.why: Reads the tilted position as a square without checking that no right angle is marked.
Uses only the parallel arrows and ignores that all four sides carry equal ticks.
Counts only one pair of sides as parallel when both pairs are marked.

questions.solution_text:
All four sides carry the same tick and both pairs of opposite sides are parallel, with no right angle marked.
Rhombus

options.why: Treats two pairs of equal sides as opposite pairs instead of adjacent pairs.
Assumes the two long sides are parallel when no parallel arrows are marked.
Treats all the tick marks as one family, so reads four equal sides.

questions.solution_text:
The two short sides are equal and meet at the top vertex; the two long sides are equal and meet at the bottom vertex.
Kite

questions.question_text:
A quadrilateral has both pairs of opposite sides parallel and equal, and none of its angles is a right angle.
Name it.

options.why: Ignores the statement that none of the angles is a right angle.
Reads "opposite sides parallel" as only one pair being parallel.
Reads the two pairs of equal sides as adjacent pairs rather than opposite pairs.

questions.solution_text:
Two pairs of parallel, equal opposite sides with no right angle is a parallelogram.
Parallelogram

questions.question_text:
All four sides of a quadrilateral are equal, and none of its angles is a right angle.
Name it.

options.why: Assumes four equal sides forces right angles, ignoring the stated condition.
Reads four equal sides as two separate pairs of adjacent equal sides.
Assumes equal sides only guarantee one pair of parallel sides.

questions.solution_text:
Four equal sides with no right angle is a rhombus.
Rhombus

questions.question_text: Which property is always true of a kite but not always true of a parallelogram?

options.text: Two pairs of adjacent sides are equal.

options.why: This is a parallelogram property; a kite’s opposite sides are unequal.

options.text: Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel.
options.why: This is a parallelogram property; a kite has no parallel sides.
Neither shape has to have four equal angles, so it separates nothing.

questions.solution_text:
A parallelogram has equal opposite sides; a kite has equal adjacent sides.
Two pairs of adjacent sides are equal.

questions.question_text: In a trapezium, which statement about the sides is always true?

options.text: At least one pair of opposite sides is parallel.
Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel.
options.why: Gives the parallelogram condition; a parallelogram is one kind of trapezium, but most trapeziums have only one parallel pair.

options.text: The two non-parallel sides are equal.
options.why: True only of an isosceles trapezium, not of every trapezium.
Confuses the trapezium with a rhombus, whose four sides are equal.

questions.solution_text:
The defining side property of a trapezium is that a pair of opposite sides is parallel. A parallelogram has a second parallel pair as well, so "both pairs" is not true of every trapezium.
At least one pair of opposite sides is parallel.

options.why: Jumps from $K$ to $M$, which are not next to each other on the shape.
Starts by skipping $L$, so the letters do not run around the shape.
Pairs $L$ with $N$, which sit on opposite corners rather than adjacent ones.

questions.solution_text:
The letters must run around the shape so that each pair of consecutive letters is an edge.
$KLMN$

questions.question_text:
Bea says that every quadrilateral with two pairs of parallel sides must be a rhombus.
Which quadrilateral shows that Bea is wrong?

options.text: A rectangle that is not a square
A rhombus that is not a square
options.why: This is an example of Bea’s claim, so it cannot disprove it.

options.text: A kite that is not a rhombus
options.why: A kite has no parallel sides, so it is not a case Bea’s claim covers.

options.text: A trapezium that is not a parallelogram
options.why: Has only one pair of parallel sides, so it is not a case Bea’s claim covers.

questions.solution_text:
A counter-example must have two pairs of parallel sides but not four equal sides.
A rectangle that is not a square has parallel opposite sides but unequal adjacent sides.
A rectangle that is not a square
